in_latin.name: Philippus
in_latin.meaning: nomen significans Philippum, civitatem in Syria, et Philippus, filius Herodi, tunc princeps Iudaeorum
in_latin.long_meaning: Nomen Philippus, quod significat Philippum, civitatem in Syria, et Philippus, filius Herodi, tunc princeps Iudaeorum, est nomen originis graecae, sed in latinitate utuntur. In Evangelio secundum Matthaeum, Philippus, unus ex discipulis Iesu, dicit eum: 'Domine, vide filium meum, qui sibi se ipse in medio sedet, et dicit eis: Ecee, filius meus, hic est qui meus est. Et dicit eis: Ecee, filius meus, hic est qui meus est.' (Mattheus 14:20-21).

In the Bible, Philip is one of Jesus' twelve apostles and is mentioned in several passages, including the Gospel of Matthew. The name has been used in various Christian cultures to signify a strong connection to the faith and a sense of nobility. In modern times, the name Philippe has become popular in countries with French influences and is often associated with qualities such as courage, loyalty, and leadership.
